facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reasonAgainst() returning a human sentence instead of a boolean. OrderStateMachine::reasonAgainst(Order, BackedEnum): ?string returns null when legal and a merchant-readable sentence when not, e.g. 'This order has already shipped. Record a return instead of cancelling it.' canTransition() is then just reasonAgainst() === null, and availableTransitions() filters on it, so the UI, the API error and the guard all share one source of truth. The same idiom drives OrderMutabilityPolicy::reasonLocked() and is the intended shape for the commission engine's explanation in P6
facts.source: Ported from SaaS-OMS and implemented in Brand New ERP P3

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reservation-based inventory with a provable invariant. stock.on_hand is signed (a real warehouse goes negative after a miscount; refusing to represent it turns a counting error into a 500). available = on_hand - reserved is DERIVED, never stored. Reserving changes only reserved; only commit changes on_hand and writes an append-only movement. Every on_hand change writes a movement carrying quantity_delta and a denormalised balance_after, so SUM(quantity_delta) == on_hand is a testable invariant per stock line. All mutations take a blocking SELECT FOR UPDATE on the stock row (not SKIP LOCKED - last-unit scarcity is queue-and-wait), and commit/release take their own lock so a reservation cannot be discharged twice
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P4; oversell reproduces on 3 of 3 runs when the lock is removed

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - attribution as its own polymorphic domain. attribution_touches is an append-only trail keyed (subject_type, subject_id, sequence); attributions holds ONE resolved row per subject and is polymorphic across Lead, Customer and Order. First touch wins for credit, but every touch is retained so last-touch and multi-touch reporting stay available and changing the credit rule is a rule change not a migration. An Order INHERITS from its lead (or the customer's own attribution) and is then FROZEN - re-attributing throws, because commission is paid on it. A converted customer inherits its lead's first touch. Unattributed is a valid first-class state, never defaulted
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P5; all 12 attribution questions answered by named tested queries

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a commission that explains itself from data. Every accrual persists rule_version_id, basis_amount, rate_type, rate_applied and a calc_inputs JSONB holding the full margin decomposition (sales, cost, shipping, fees, allocated ad spend, each with a label and a human basis string). explain() then RENDERS that line rather than storing prose: 'Commission MYR 38.50 - Recipient: Ali (marketer) - Rule: "Facebook Campaign Margin" v1 (effective 2025-08-15) - 12% of MYR 320.80 - Sales MYR 1,000.00 - Cost MYR 520.00 - Shipping MYR 49.20 - Fees MYR 30.00 - Ads MYR 80.00 = MYR 320.80 - Order SO-00001 - Provisional'. Rule versions are immutable (DB trigger) and effective-dated, so a closed period can never be rewritten, and commissions are never deleted - a reversal is a contra entry with negated amount AND negated sources so the trail nets to zero
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P6; 23 tests covering all ten prior-art anti-patterns

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a minimal but real double-entry ledger for an SME ERP. accounts (asset/liability/equity/income/expense) + journal_entries + journal_lines. Balance is enforced three ways: the Ledger service refuses an unbalanced post with a readable message, a CHECK constraint requires total_debit = total_credit on the entry, and a per-line CHECK requires exactly one of debit or credit to be positive. journal_lines are append-only at the DB (UPDATE and DELETE both rejected) so corrections must be reversing entries. balanceOf() signs by account type and trialBalance() must always be zero - that single assertion catches almost every posting mistake. Commission flows through it properly: payable posts Dr Commission Expense / Cr Commission Payable, and the payout posts Dr Commission Payable / Cr Bank, so the payable account clears to zero
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P7; 19 tests including trial-balance assertions after issue, payment, void and payout

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - precomputed rollups verified by an INDEPENDENT live oracle. The rollup is built by SQL GROUP BY; the oracle recomputes the same figures by iterating orders in PHP with exact decimal Money arithmetic. Because the two paths share no code, comparing them is a real cross-check rather than a tautology - a planted bug (summing unit_cost without multiplying by quantity) is caught immediately. The comparison also proves freshness: rebuilding is idempotent (delete-then-insert per slice, asserted by rebuilding three times) and a cancelled order drops out on rebuild. The rollup slice key uses UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT so unattributed slices cannot silently duplicate
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P8; oracle catches a planted aggregation bug on the first run

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - landed cost that cannot double-count. Freight/duty/handling are recorded as goods_receipt_costs rows with an allocation rule (by_value, by_quantity, by_weight); the allocator apportions each pool across receipt lines and writes landed_unit_cost plus a landed_cost_basis JSONB holding every component, its share, its per-unit effect and a human explanation. The variant's average_cost is then RECOMPUTED FROM THE FULL RECEIPT HISTORY rather than maintained incrementally, which makes re-application idempotent by construction - no reversal bookkeeping, no drift. Order lines snapshot average_cost when it exists and record unit_cost_source so a margin figure can always say whether it rests on a real receipt or a typed guess
facts.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP after P9; 9 tests, both allocation modes proven distinct by mutation

facts.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a restore rehearsal that runs on a schedule. erp:backup dumps, prunes to a retention window and optionally copies offsite; erp:verify-backup restores the NEWEST dump into a scratch database, compares table/trigger/CHECK/foreign-key counts against the live schema, PROVES the restored copy still refuses a journal edit by inserting a real row and attempting to update it, drops the scratch database, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. Scheduled weekly, because a restore verified once decays. Three hardening details found by actually running it: a failed dump must delete its own partial file or a truncated file looks like a backup; filenames need a random suffix or two runs in the same second overwrite each other; and enabling offsite without a command must be a hard error
facts.source: Implemented and run in Brand New ERP; detected a genuine schema-drift mismatch 107/106 tables on an outdated dump
